- *The Lamb is its lamp*: Jesus is the light of the world (see {{John 8:12|John 8:12}}; {{John 9:5|9:5}}; {{John 12:35-36|12:35–36}}).

- *the nations*: God’s promise to Abraham comes true ({{Genesis 12:3|Genesis 12:3}}; see {{Isaiah 2:3|Isaiah 2:3}}). 

- In Revelation, the kings of the world often represent God’s enemies ({{Revelation 6:15|Revelation 6:15}}; {{Revelation 17:18|17:18}}; {{Revelation 18:3|18:3}}, {{Revelation 18:9|9}}). Now that these enemies are destroyed ({{Revelation 16:9|Revelation 16:9}}, {{Revelation 16:11|11}}; {{Revelation 19:1-2|19:1–2}}, {{Revelation 19:19-21|19–21}}), the image is of God’s glory shown in those who have repented ({{Revelation 14:6-7|Revelation 14:6–7}}; compare {{Revelation 11:13|11:13}}) and walk with God ({{Revelation 5:9|5:9}}; {{Revelation 15:4|15:4}}). 

- The gates that are never closed contrast with ancient times when closed gates protected cities from enemies, especially at night. The people experience peace and security under God’s rule (see {{Isaiah 60:11|Isaiah 60:11}}). God’s enemies are gone, and fear and failure have ended (see {{Zechariah 14:7|Zechariah 14:7}}; {{John 11:8-10|John 11:8–10}}; {{John 12:35-36|12:35–36}}).

*unclean*: Spiritual impurity is a key concern in Revelation (see {{Revelation 21:8|Revelation 21:8}}). Here, evil includes idolatry and dishonesty (see {{Revelation 14:5|Revelation 14:5}}; {{Revelation 21:8|21:8}}; {{Revelation 22:15|22:15}}). Those not listed in the *Book of Life* cannot enter the city of God. Only those with names in the *Book of Life*, the pure of heart ({{Matthew 5:8|Matthew 5:8}}), will see God.

This part of John's vision of the city shows how God provides water and food for his people (compare {{Exodus 16:4|Exodus 16:4}}, {{Exodus 16:22-24|22–24}}; {{Ezekiel 47:1-12|Ezekiel 47:1–12}}; {{John 4:10|John 4:10}}; {{John 6:32-35|6:32–35}}). God first created a "garden of delight" (Eden) for Adam and Eve, but they disobeyed him and lost it ({{Genesis 2:1-3:24|Genesis 2–3}}). Now, Eden is remade and joined with the heavenly city as God's wonderful gift for his faithful people.

After humans sinned, they lost access to the tree of life (see {{Genesis 3:22-24|Genesis 3:22–24}}), but now it is freely available. The tree stands on each side of the river (compare {{Ezekiel 47:12|Ezekiel 47:12}}), showing there is no wrong side of the river in heaven. The tree produces fresh fruit every month, demonstrating God's constant provision.

- *No longer … any curse*: Since the first sin ({{Genesis 3:14-19|Genesis 3:14–19}}), humanity has faced a curse due to their rebellion against God (see {{1 Corinthians 16:22|1 Corinthians 16:22}}). Now, rebellion, sin, and the curse are gone forever. 

- *His servants will worship him*: Revelation shows examples of true worship (see {{Revelation 4:1-5:14|Revelation 4–5}}; {{Revelation 7:9-17|7:9–17}}).

The fear of death and seeing God will disappear (see {{Genesis 16:13|Genesis 16:13}}; {{Genesis 32:30|32:30}}; {{Judges 6:22|Judges 6:22}}; {{Isaiah 6:5|Isaiah 6:5}}). God's people will carry his name and joyfully see his face (see {{Matthew 5:8|Matthew 5:8}}; {{2 Corinthians 3:18|2 Corinthians 3:18}}; {{1 John 3:2-3|1 John 3:2–3}}).

They will rule with God forever (see {{Revelation 20:4|Revelation 20:4}}; see also {{Revelation 5:10|5:10}}) in his bright light that removes night and the need for lamps (see {{Isaiah 60:19-20|Isaiah 60:19–20}}).

Everything John records in Revelation is trustworthy and true because God, who has all authority (compare {{Matthew 28:18|Matthew 28:18}}), sent the messenger. However, these visions are not easy to understand.

An angel made it clear that the visions John had seen were from God. This filled John with so much wonder that he tried to worship the angel. But the angel reminded John that only God was to be worshipped.

He also told John to share the words of the prophecy he had been given. Three times John recorded Jesus’ promises about his return. Jesus also invited everyone to wash their robes. This was a way of talking about people no longer living in their old ways. Instead they were to follow Jesus’ example for living.

When people trust in Jesus, they can eat freely from the tree of life. The Holy Spirit and the church invite everyone to come to Jesus. Then people can drink freely of the water of life.

John urged the believers to pay attention to the prophecy he had written down. Hearing it and turning to God would bring blessing. John said Amen to Jesus’ promise to come back to earth. John closed his letter to the churches in Asia with a blessing about Jesus’ grace.

This epilogue to Revelation includes words from an angel ({{Revelation 22:6|Revelation 22:6}}, {{Revelation 22:8-11|8–11}}) and Christ ({{Revelation 22:7|22:7}}, {{Revelation 22:12-19|12–19}}). It ends with a plea for Christ’s return ({{Revelation 22:20|Revelation 22:20}}) and a final blessing ({{Revelation 22:21|22:21}}). The epilogue connects directly with the book's introduction ({{Revelation 1:1-11|Revelation 1:1–11}}). It highlights key themes such as: 

- encouraging faithful perseverance,

- warning those who do evil things,

- affirming the truth of the prophetic message, and

- restating the nearness of Christ’s return.

*Blessed*: The sixth blessing in Revelation (see {{Revelation 1:3|Revelation 1:3}}; {{Revelation 14:13|14:13}}; {{Revelation 16:15|16:15}}; {{Revelation 19:9|19:9}}; {{Revelation 20:6|20:6}}; {{Revelation 22:14|22:14}}) is for those who obey. Obedience is essential for God's blessing.

The warning against false worship (see {{Revelation 19:10|Revelation 19:10}}) is repeated when John falls at the angel's feet again. Only God deserves our worship (compare John the Baptist's relationship to Jesus; {{John 1:6-8|John 1:6–8}}, {{John 1:26-27|26–27}}; {{John 3:27-35|3:27–35}}).

*Do not seal up*: The angel expands John's initial instruction to *Write on a scroll* ({{Revelation 1:11|Revelation 1:11}}) and warns against limiting its communication. Although some things are sealed, God does not reveal everything (compare {{Revelation 10:4|Revelation 10:4}}). What has been written must be shared so people understand the message's seriousness and that the time is near (see {{Revelation 1:1|Revelation 1:1}}, {{Revelation 1:3|3}}; {{Revelation 22:6-7|22:6–7}}; compare {{Daniel 12:4|Daniel 12:4}}).

People who refuse to accept God's forgiveness will remain wicked (see {{Revelation 16:9|Revelation 16:9}}). John reminds good people to keep their integrity. This verse warns wrongdoers and urges the righteous to understand the importance of Christ's return for their commitments and actions.

Christ is coming soon to repay everyone, not just based on their faith, but according to their actions (see {{Revelation 2:23|Revelation 2:23}}; {{Revelation 11:18|11:18}}; {{Revelation 14:13|14:13}}; {{Revelation 20:12-13|20:12–13}}; see also {{Proverbs 24:12|Proverbs 24:12}}; {{Matthew 16:27|Matthew 16:27}}; {{2 Corinthians 5:10|2 Corinthians 5:10}}). Not every statement of belief is sincere ({{John 2:23-25|John 2:23–25}}); true faith shows through actions ({{James 2:14-26|James 2:14–26}}). We are saved by God's grace and power in Christ. Our actions do not save us, but they show the seriousness of our confession and provide a fair basis for our final reward or punishment.

- *Blessed are those*: In response to the link between actions and final outcomes ({{Revelation 22:12|Revelation 22:12}}), the seventh blessing of Revelation (see also {{Revelation 1:3|1:3}}; {{Revelation 14:13|14:13}}; {{Revelation 16:15|16:15}}; {{Revelation 19:9|19:9}}; {{Revelation 20:6|20:6}}; {{Revelation 22:7|22:7}}) promises acceptance for those who wash their robes. These are people purified by trusting in Christ and following him faithfully ({{Revelation 3:5|Revelation 3:5}}; {{Revelation 6:11|6:11}}; {{Revelation 7:9-10|7:9–10}}, {{Revelation 7:14|14}}; {{Revelation 19:13|19:13}}; {{Ephesians 5:26|Ephesians 5:26}}; {{Hebrews 10:22|Hebrews 10:22}}). 

- *enter the city by its gates*: See study note on Revelation 21:24–25.

- This verse lists those not allowed to enter, contrasting with those admitted in {{Revelation 22:14|Revelation 22:14}} (see {{Revelation 21:8|21:8}}, {{Revelation 21:27|27}}; {{Revelation 22:11|22:11}}). Unrepentant sinners stay outside the city. It warns that those who do not repent cannot enter the city of God ({{Revelation 22:14|Revelation 22:14}}). 

- The term *dogs* for sinners was a common Jewish label for outsiders (see {{Matthew 7:6|Matthew 7:6}}; {{Philippians 3:2|Philippians 3:2}}; also {{2 Samuel 3:8|2 Samuel 3:8}}; {{2 Kings 8:13|2 Kings 8:13}}); Jews used this term for Gentiles (see {{Mark 7:26-28|Mark 7:26–28}}).

- *I am the Root and the Offspring of David*: Jesus confirms the message of Revelation (compare {{John 21:24|John 21:24}}). He is the *Root of David* (see {{Revelation 5:5|Revelation 5:5}}; {{Isaiah 11:10|Isaiah 11:10}}) and a *descendant of David* (see {{Ezekiel 37:23-24|Ezekiel 37:23–24}}; {{Romans 1:3|Romans 1:3}}). 

- The morning star was a title for the Messiah (see {{Numbers 24:17|Numbers 24:17}}; {{2 Peter 1:19|2 Peter 1:19}}; compare {{Luke 1:78-79|Luke 1:78–79}}).

- *Come* is a repeated invitation and a confession (see {{Revelation 22:20|Revelation 22:20}}). 

- *the bride*: The Lamb’s wife (see {{Revelation 21:9|Revelation 21:9}}), represents the church, the people of God. 

- The thirsty can drink freely from God's provision (see {{Revelation 21:6|Revelation 21:6}}; {{Revelation 22:1|22:1}}; {{Psalm 42:1|Psalm 42:1}}; {{Isaiah 55:1|Isaiah 55:1}}; {{John 4:10-14|John 4:10–14}}).

- *I testify*: John swears to protect the integrity of the Book of Revelation. He curses anyone who changes the book's content or message (compare {{Deuteronomy 4:2|Deuteronomy 4:2}}; {{Deuteronomy 12:32|12:32}}). This curse contrasts with the blessing for those who read aloud, listen to, and follow the prophecy ({{Revelation 1:3|Revelation 1:3}}). When Revelation was written, scribes sometimes changed books to fit their views. Early Christians quickly developed ways to verify messages and messengers (see {{John 21:24|John 21:24}}; {{1 Corinthians 16:21|1 Corinthians 16:21}}; {{Galatians 6:11|Galatians 6:11}}; {{Colossians 4:18|Colossians 4:18}}; {{2 Thessalonians 3:17|2 Thessalonians 3:17}}; {{1 John 4:1-3|1 John 4:1–3}}). 

- Since the early church, the New Testament's scope and content have defined Christian teachings. However, some still try to change Scripture by adding works they consider equal to the Bible or by claiming parts of the Bible are unreliable. The true church has rejected and will continue to reject these attempts to change the canon, viewing them as human or even demonic efforts to alter the foundation of the Christian faith.

- *I am coming soon*: See {{Revelation 3:11|Revelation 3:11}}. 

- *Come, Lord Jesus!*: Paul expressed the same wish ({{1 Corinthians 16:22|1 Corinthians 16:22}}; see also {{Philippians 4:5|Philippians 4:5}}).

- Revelation ends with a blessing similar to those in Paul's letters (for example, {{Romans 15:33|Romans 15:33}}; {{1 Corinthians 16:23-24|1 Corinthians 16:23–24}}). 

- The final sentence fittingly calls upon the grace of the Lord Jesus, which is the foundation of our forgiveness and the basis of our eternal hope.
